notes: 'Sozinho' agrees in gender and number with the person it describes ('sozinho', 'sozinha', 'sozinhos', 'sozinhas'), even when translated as 'by oneself' or 'on one's own'.
Do not confuse with 'só', which can also mean 'alone' but most often means 'only' ('só um' = only one).

faults.quote: Ele sente-se muito sozinho na cidade grande.
faults.why: Enclisis ('sente-se') after a subject pronoun is unnatural in Brazilian Portuguese; use proclisis ('se sente').
Merely restates the two senses; better to note how 'sozinho' also means 'without help'.
